units.q1: Why shouldn't a severely hypothermic, confused person be rewarmed quickly in the field?
units.a1:
Hypothermia (very cold, shivering, confused or drowsy): get them indoors or to a sheltered place as quickly as possible, out of the wind and off the cold ground. Remove wet clothing and wrap them in dry blankets, a sleeping bag or towels, with the head covered. Handle them gently. If they're fully awake, give a warm non-alcoholic drink and something sugary like chocolate; give no drinks to someone who isn't fully awake. You can also warm them skin to skin under dry blankets. Don't use a hot bath, hot-water bottle, heat lamp or fire, don't rub their arms, legs, hands or feet, and don't give alcohol. If they stop breathing normally, start CPR and keep warming them. Call emergency services for anyone you think has hypothermia; don't drive them yourself if an ambulance can come.

Source: NHS, Hypothermia; St John Ambulance (UK), Hypothermia; CDC, Preventing Hypothermia. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
